prompt: The cyclopentadienyl anion (C5H5⁻) is aromatic. Why does cyclopentadiene (C5H6, neutral) tend to lose a proton more easily (pKa ~16) than typical hydrocarbons (pKa ~44)?

options.label: The resulting anion is aromatic (6 π e⁻ in the planar 5-ring) — huge stabilization
The sp3 CH₂ H's are polarized
The ring strain pushes H out

explanation: Deprotonating the sp3 CH₂ gives Cp⁻ with 6 π e⁻ in a planar 5-ring: aromatic! That aromatic stabilization lowers the pKa by ~28 units (16 vs 44 for cyclopentane). Compare: cycloheptatriene has pKa ~44 (losing H gives antiaromatic 8 π e⁻), while cycloheptatrienyl cation is super-stabilized (6 π e⁻).
